entries.reason: Revised after transform-review-G.json refused the first transform. 1 carrier (ENG-003-A-CZ-A7, 'If we painted a picture on every lid, people ___ exactly where things go.'), 3 carrying options. Pass 2 on the original: the hint covers only will/would, and two carrying options ('would have known', 'would be knowing') already use 'would'. My first addition ('Use 'would have' only when the if part has 'had'') is FALSE as grammar: mixed conditionals put 'would have' after an if part with no 'had' ('If I were braver, I would have gone'). The revised move makes no only-if claim; it tells the child what each form means. (a) In an imagined if, a past form without 'had' ('if we painted') refers to now or later, not the past (second conditional). (b) 'Would have' imagines the past. Each claim describes its own clause, so mixed conditionals do not break them ('If I were braver' is about now; 'I would have gone' is about the past). That reaches 'would have known': the if part is about now or later, so a past result does not fit. 'Would be knowing' CANNOT be covered by a general move. Its fault is that 'know' is a state verb and takes no -ing here, but the description's impossible-form half has several shapes ('would knew', 'would be knowing'), and one sentence naming 'know' would teach one verb. So the revised hint serves 2 of 3 carrying options. If a person wants the third, an optional sentence would be 'Some verbs, like know, do not usually take -ing.' (true as grammar; not proposed, since it takes the hint to five sentences for one option).
